newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand pushes mergers of weak finance firms.
newsitem.headline: Thailand pushes mergers of weak finance firms.

text.p: The Thai central bank said on Wednesday it was seeking ways get weak finance and securities firms it takes under its wings to merge to ease troubles in the ailing sector.
Analysts favouring greater consolidation and efficiency in the sector applauded the Bank of Thailand's plan and said it would bring greater stability to the turmoil-ridden industry.

As part of efforts to support the flagging sector, the central bank earlier this month identified 10 weakened finance firms hit by liquidity crunches and as part of a major revamp told them to increase their capital.
Any new shares the firms failed to sell as part of their capital increase plan were to be bought by the central bank.

Two of three listed companies named, Sri Dhana Finance and Securities and Dynamic Eastern Finance Thailand Plc, have already said the Bank of Thailand support fund would take stakes in them after their new share issues.
Another of the 10 firms told to to raise capital, ITF Finance and Securities, announced a 1.30 billion baht rights issue on Monday.
But with the central bank's minority stake insufficient to force consolidations, the bank is looking at alternatives.

"I think there will have to be other incentives because we won't be the major shareholders in these companies. It might be incentives to carry out certain activities, which have yet to be worked out," said bank spokeswoman Duangmanee Vrongprathip.
The Bank of Thailand would seek to coax firms that remain resistant to consolidation, she said.
"Maybe for financial institutions that don't merge there could be even more stringent measures later on to ensure stability," the spokeswoman said.
More compulsory capital increases in the sector were possible, she said, though further naming of ailing finance firms was unlikely in the short term.
"It's a cleansing process that needs to be done at some stage so the sooner its starts the better," said Ian Mclellan, head of research at SBC Warburg.
"What the Bank of Thailand and the government have done in the last month is positive. It's not changed sentiment yet but it is heading in the right direction," Mclellan said.
How receptive the named firms are to consolidation varies. Dynamic Eastern Managing Director Suchart Boonbangjerdsri has previously indicated his willingness to consider offers.
The case for others is less clear cut.

"If you ask me whether a merger is possible, I think it is in the long term it is possible, but a merger is not something that happens overnight...we have to find compatible partners," said Chatchawin Charoen-Rajapark, president of Sri Dhana Finance and Securities.
"It will be on a voluntary basis, and a basis of mutual benefits for the merging partners," he said.
For Sri Dhana, which opposed the central bank's decision to place it on the watch list, the issue has been damaged confidence, which will take time to restore.
"We feel it is quite unjustified they put our name on the list. It's a miscommunication that has caused problems for Sri Dhana and repairs will take some time," he said.

But the Bank of Thailand's approach has won praise from analysts who believe consolidation must trim the country's 91 finance firms to around half its current number if investor confidence is to be restored.
